combining_packages: Several Scout packages may be pasted together. Match them by track.name: a Base and a Post with the same name are one processing chain (Post minus Base = what the effects did); different names are different tracks of the same mix. Analyze whatever set is present.

analysis_request.user_question: What processing would you suggest for this track?

interpretation_guide.lufs_reference: EBU R128, target varies by genre (-14 LUFS streaming, -16 broadcast)
interpretation_guide.delta_meaning: post minus base; positive = boost, negative = cut
interpretation_guide.crest_factor: Peak minus RMS in dB; lower = more compressed
interpretation_guide.true_peak: Inter-sample peak in dBTP; streaming target <= -1 dBTP
interpretation_guide.loudness_range: EBU LRA in LU; macro-dynamics across the capture, higher = more dynamic
interpretation_guide.spectral_centroid: Brightness center of mass in Hz (band-energy weighted); higher = brighter
interpretation_guide.low_freq_correlation: Phase coherence below 150 Hz; negative = bass phase issues
interpretation_guide.tilt_db_per_octave: Slope of the 63 Hz-10 kHz spectrum in 1/3-octave bands: 0 = pink-noise balance, typical mixed material -1 to -3, more negative = darker, positive = brighter than pink
interpretation_guide.resonances_above_trend: Bands standing above the tilt line; candidates for narrow EQ cuts
interpretation_guide.side_to_mid_db: Side energy relative to mid; null = mono, around -6 to -12 dB is moderate width
interpretation_guide.noise_floor_p10_dbfs: RMS of the quietest 10% of 10 ms windows

loudness_distribution.note: percentiles of 400 ms K-weighted blocks above the -70 LUFS gate; p90 minus p10 is the working dynamic span

scout_flags.message: Spectral tilt 0.68 dB/oct - brighter than pink
794 Hz stands 14.0 dB above the trend - possible resonance

known_limitations: Spectrum uses 31 one-third-octave IIR bandpass filters (not FFT) - coarse but zero-latency
LUFS/LRA use a close BS.1770 approximation (biquad K-weighting), not a certified meter
True peak uses 4x Hermite interpolation - an estimate, not the BS.1770 FIR
Transient detection uses fixed 10ms-window RMS comparison, not sample-accurate onset detection
Single capture window - does not represent full song dynamics
Stereo width is correlation-based estimate, not full spatial analysis

ai_response_instructions.style: Thorough analysis with reasoning. Reference specific measurements, explain trade-offs, suggest parameter ranges.
constraints: Reference specific numeric values from the data
Suggest specific parameter ranges when recommending adjustments
Consider the track role when evaluating if processing is appropriate
If a Base and Post package share a name, evaluate what the chain did and whether it helps or hurts
If several tracks are present, consider how they interact; if asked for rough-mix levels or pans, give a per-track table: fader offset in dB relative to the loudest track, pan, one-line reason
avoid: Do not recommend specific plugin brands unless asked
Do not repeat back raw numbers without interpretation
Do not explain what measurements mean - the user is an audio engineer

preset_for_clean_q.when: Whenever you recommend EQ for a track, end the reply with ONE ```json block per track in exactly this format, so it pastes straight into the Clean Q equalizer. Leave it out if you recommend no EQ.
rules: type: bell | lowshelf | highshelf | lowcut | highcut | notch | bandpass
freq in Hz; gain in dB, -30..30, bells and shelves only; q 0.025..40 (shelves and cuts: 0.7)
optional per band: "channel": stereo | left | right | mid | side; "dynamic": { "on": true, "threshold": -24, "range": -4 } for a band that only moves when the level crosses the threshold
bands are moves to make; markers are spots worth checking by ear -- Clean Q draws them as guides the engineer can click to turn into a band
at most 24 bands; numbers must come from the measurements in this package
